headline: Dry weather ends Wednesday evening, then a windier, wetter pattern starts Friday and likely continues into next week.
summary: Tuesday is mostly dry with a mix of clouds and sunshine, though a few showers near Mount Rainier should fade by evening. Dry weather holds into Wednesday morning. A weak front (the leading edge of an incoming weather system) then brings rain to the lowlands Wednesday evening into Thursday, with locally breezy winds from around Whidbey Island northward. Thursday afternoon should be mostly dry in the lowlands, with some lingering rain or drizzle in the mountains, and highs stay in the mid to upper 50s through Thursday. A more active pattern begins Friday, when a stronger front brings lowland rain and gusty south winds. The strongest winds are expected along the immediate coast and from Admiralty Inlet northward, and forecasters are still deciding whether to issue wind alerts for Friday. Saturday brings a warm front with rain at times for the Olympic Peninsula and near the Canadian border, and a brief drier spell for some of Puget Sound. A cold front then crosses Saturday night into Sunday with more rain and breezy winds. Because many trees still have leaves, localized power outages are possible during this stretch. Snow levels, the elevation where rain turns to snow, stay high, mainly 5000 to 8000 feet from Friday into Sunday, so snow is limited to high elevations. Computer model runs suggest a possible short break in the heavier precipitation from Sunday night into Monday, but that is only a suggestion. Another front is expected late Monday, and next week looks to bring more lowland rain, mountain snow, gusty winds, and large waves, though details will likely change. Seas on the coast are expected to build toward 15 to 20 feet starting Friday, and forecasters are watching for high surf. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will start to saturate the soil and raise river levels, which could become a concern with later storms. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for land areas of western Washington. Small Craft Advisories for boaters are in effect on the coastal waters through Wednesday.
